thesis: Scaling dense Transformers pretrained on internet-scale text produces increasingly general capability.

bindingConstraint.description: Frontier capability is limited by available accelerator compute and the capital to buy it, not by known algorithmic ideas.

layers.paradigm: Large fleets of general-purpose GPU accelerators (NVIDIA A100 class)
layers.assumption: Frontier capability requires large accelerator clusters, with general-purpose GPUs as the practical default.

distribution.basis: training hardware of 8 frontier-scale runs described publicly 2020-2021 — GPT-3, Megatron-Turing NLG, Jurassic-1, Megatron-LM (GPU); Gopher, LaMDA, GLaM, Switch Transformer (TPU)

layers.assumption: Attention-based Transformer architectures are the dominant path to frontier general capability.

distribution.basis: architecture family of frontier-scale models released 2020-2021; every one publicly described is attention-based

evidence: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces (S4) — 2021-10

layers.paradigm: Self-supervised next-token pretraining, then supervised fine-tuning
layers.assumption: General capability comes from next-token prediction at scale; task behaviour is then elicited by fine-tuning on labelled examples.
frontier: code pretraining as a reasoning substrate
evidence: Learning to summarize from human feedback, OpenAI — 2020-09
Show Your Work: Scratchpads for Intermediate Computation — 2021-11
A General Language Assistant as a Laboratory for Alignment, Anthropic — 2021-12
FLAN: Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners — 2021-09
Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code (Codex) — 2021-07
no frontier model of this period shipped preference post-training — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Internet-scale web crawl plus curated text corpora
layers.assumption: Enough high-quality text exists on the open web, and more of it reliably improves capability.
frontier: retrieval from a corpus instead of memorising it
evidence: Common Crawl as primary pretraining source, GPT-3 — 2020-05
Deduplicating Training Data Makes Language Models Better — 2021-07
no defensible share data for this layer as of the cutoff — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Parameter-count scaling under the Kaplan exponents
layers.assumption: Capability follows model size and compute at predictable exponents; parameters are the scarce input to buy.
frontier: sparse scaling — more parameters at constant compute
evidence: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models, Kaplan et al. — 2020-01
GLaM, 1.2T sparse params at ~1/3 GPT-3 training energy — 2021-12
NOTE: no public argument for token-count-optimal training exists as of this date
no public source apportions frontier compute by scaling strategy — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Fixed short context window; weights frozen after training
layers.assumption: Everything task-specific must fit in a short context window, and nothing persists between calls.
evidence: context length is a property of the paradigm, not a share of it — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Programmatic API access for developers; research code for everyone else
layers.assumption: Frontier models are reached through APIs and code by technical users; there is no general consumer surface.
evidence: no public source apportions usage across API, research code and product surfaces — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Eight-to-nine-figure training runs; closed weights monetised as API rent
layers.assumption: Frontier capability requires capital that only a handful of organisations command.

distribution.basis: weight availability of 6 frontier-scale models released 2020-2021 — GPT-3, Gopher, LaMDA, Jurassic-1, Megatron-Turing NLG (closed); GPT-J-6B (open)

evidence: GPT-3 available by API only, weights unreleased — 2020-05
